note: Declared correspondence between each participant's own refusal vocabulary and the kernel refusal it realizes. SPEC.md admits reference implementations only as participants tested against the contract, so the fifth acceptance criterion on issue #6 is met by proving the participants already decide the same way on the same fact, not by rewriting them into the kernel. A correspondence declared here is checked by driving both sides and comparing their decisions; a participant that stops agreeing fails the check rather than quietly diverging.

participants.note: Enforces lease fencing, expiry, and the separation of report from observation in SQL. Driven for real by the parity check against a temporary store.

correspondences.fact: a superseded fence may not report
an executor report is not settlement
correspondences.participant_refusal: RuntimeError:run has no independently observable report
correspondences.note: The participant refuses observation of a run that never reported; the kernel refuses a report that asks to settle itself. Both refuse the same move from opposite ends.

participants.note: Carries its own standing transition table for coordination tickets. Driven by evaluating its own requests against its own table.

correspondences.fact: the actor that built an artifact may not witness it
an actor without judgement authority may not ratify
correspondences.note: The participant splits one kernel refusal into two names by target: OWNER_RATIFICATION_REQUIRED when the target is RATIFIED, OWNER_JUDGEMENT_REQUIRED for any other owner-reserved transition. The kernel makes no such distinction. A finer participant vocabulary over the same kernel refusal is permitted; a coarser one that admitted what the kernel refuses would not be.

correspondences.fact: an external effect outside every declared scope is refused
correspondences.note: Both sides read the same authorization contract, so both name the refusal the same way. What changed is that the refusal is now over a scope rather than over an effect class.

correspondences.fact: a declared precondition on an admitted verb must be discharged
correspondences.note: Both sides read scopes[].preconditions from the same authorization contract and refuse the same move, and they are written separately so this check compares two implementations rather than one shared function. The participant names the finer code the contract declares; the kernel keeps the single code it already uses for every way an effect can fall outside its authorization. A finer participant vocabulary over one kernel refusal is permitted, as it already is for ratification.

participants.note: Enforces the proposal requirement on model claims and the live-grant check on every transition. Driven for real by the parity check against a temporary journal.

correspondences.fact: a model claim without a proposal is incomplete
correspondences.note: The participant refuses a MODEL post that claims while carrying no proposal_id; the kernel refuses a submit_proposal whose required fields are absent. Both refuse the same move: a model assertion entering the record with nothing behind it that can be read back. Declared against MISSING_PRECONDITION rather than INCOMPLETE_PROPOSAL because that is what the kernel actually decides here - contracts/kernel-transitions.json lists INCOMPLETE_PROPOSAL under submit_proposal, but scripts/sovkernel/transitions.py emits MISSING_PRECONDITION for every absent precondition and emits INCOMPLETE_PROPOSAL nowhere. Recorded as OPEN-SEAMS rather than papered over; a parity correspondence must name the refusal the kernel produces, not the one it advertises.

correspondences.fact: no live grant covers this transition
correspondences.note: The participant checks a typed, scoped, live grant at every console transition; the kernel checks the same thing at retract. The transitions differ, the fact does not, and a participant that admitted an ungranted actor would diverge here.
